svg.title: Architecture Tricks Diagram
svg.desc: Compares common architecture tricks such as tied embeddings and Gemma-style RMSNorm scaling.
svg.text: Architecture tricks: small changes, large effects
Two common examples: tied word embeddings and Gemma-style RMSNorm scaling
input embeddings and lm_head share parameters
reduces parameter count and aligns input/output semantics
often used in GPT / Qwen-style models
scaling form changes from w to (1 + w)
gives a smoother early training path
- they do not change the main block structure
- they do change parameter flow and early optimization behavior
- they are easy to miss if you only look at the high-level architecture
- they matter when comparing code paths across model families
This page is the place to collect these small but meaningful deviations
It keeps the main model pages focused on core structure while preserving important implementation quirks
